msItem.explicit: ተተርጐመት፡ ዛቲ፡ መጽሐፍ፡ አምሳነ፡ ዓረቢ፡ በግዕዝ፡ በአፈ፡ ሚካኤል፡ ዘይንዕስ። ወልደ፡ ወልዱ፡ ለጊዮርጊስ፡ ወልደ፡ አባ፡ ሚካኤል፡ ጳጳስ።

colophon.foreign: ዛቲ፡ መጽሐፍ፡ ተጽሕፈት፡ በዘመነ፡ መንግሥቱ፡ ለብሩሃ፡ አእምሮ፡ ንጉሥነ፡ ኃይለ፡ ሥላሴ፡ ወበዘመነ፡ ምልክናሁ፡ ለርቱዓ፡ ፍትሕ፡ ደጃዝማች፡ ኃይለ፡ ሥላሴ፡ በ፲ወ፱፻፳፮ ዓመት፡ እምልደተ፡ እግዚእነ፡ ኢየሱስ፡ ክርስቶስ፡ ወጸሐፊሁ፡ ጸዋሬ፡ ስም፡ አባ፡ ተክለ፡ ሃይማኖት። ዝመጽሐፍ፡ ዘልዕልት፡ ወይዘሮ፡ ገዛችን፡ ወስመ፡ ጥምቀታ፡ ወለተ፡ ማርያም፡ ወወሀበታ፡ ለኪዳነ፡ መሕረት፡ ማየ፡ አንበሳ፡ ከመ፡ ይኩና፡ መርሃ፡ ለመንግሥተ፡ ሰማያት። ወኢያርእያ፡ ዘበምድር፡ ኃዘናት፡ ዘሠረቆ፡ ወዘፈሐቆ፡ ውጉዝ፡ ውእቱ፡ በሥልጣነ፡ ሐዋርያት።

This book was written during the reign of our king, the enlightened Ḫāyla Śǝllāse and during the rulership of the just daǧǧāzmāč Ḫāyla Śǝllāse in the year 1926 from the birth of Our Lord Jesus Christ and its scribe bears the name ʾAbbā Takla Hāymānot. This book is of Lǝʿǝlt Wayzaro Gazzāččǝn and her baptismal name is Walatta Māryām; she gave (the book) to Kidāna Mǝḥrat May ʾAnbasā so that it might be her guide to the Kingdom of Heavens, so that He would not show her the sorrows of the earth. The one who steals it or that scratches it shall be cursed by the authority of the Apostles.
colophon.note: The colophon states that the manuscript was written during the reign of King Ḫāyla Śǝllāse in 1926 A.M (= 1933/34 A.D.), when Rās Ḫāyla Śǝllāse Gugsā held office. It was written by ʾAbbā Takla Hāymānot. The manuscript was donated to Māy ʾAnbasā Dabra Gannat Kidāna Mǝḥrat by Wayzaro Gazzāččǝn.

origin.origDate: According to , the manuscript was completed in 1926 A.M (= 1933/34 A.D.)

history.provenance:
According to , the manuscript was donated to Māy ʾAnbasā Dabra Gannat Kidāna Mǝḥrat by Wayzaro Gazzāččǝn Gabra Ḥǝywat (her father’s name is provided in ). She was likely connected with the family of Rās Ḫayla Śǝllāse Gugsā. Her baptismal name, Walatta Māryām, appears in many supplication formulas, e.g. on .
The late Emperor Yoḥannǝs IV and his “children” (most likely not all of them were his biological children): ʾArʾayā Śǝllāse, Walda Giyorgis, Ḫāyla Śǝllāse and Ṣǝge Māryām appear in a supplication formula on . Their names also appear in other supplication formulas throughout the manuscript: Walda Giyorgis ; Ṣǝge Māryām ; Ḫāyla Śǝllāse; Walatta Kiros . A number of other people associated with her family appear in the legends of the miniatures.
